questions.stem:
"Stop taking this medicine and tell your doctor immediately if you notice any of the following rare side effects: swelling of the face, lips or throat, difficulty breathing, or a severe skin rash with blistering. Common side effects include nausea and headache. Uncommon side effects include dizziness and sleep disturbance. The frequency of certain other effects cannot be determined based on available data."

From the informational leaflet for a prescription antihistamine

Which of the following statements is the correct interpretation of the information contained in this excerpt?
options: A patient who develops a blistering skin rash while taking this medicine should stop taking it and contact a doctor immediately.
Nausea is a rarer side effect of this medicine than a severe skin rash.
Difficulty breathing is a common side effect of this medicine.
Every patient who takes this medicine experiences at least one side effect.
Sleep disturbance is a reason to stop the medicine immediately.
questions.exp: The leaflet places a severe blistering rash in the group of rare effects for which the instruction is to stop the medicine and tell a doctor immediately, so the matching interpretation is the one about the blistering rash. Nausea is listed as common, so calling it rarer than the rash reverses the frequency ranking, and difficulty breathing belongs to the rare, urgent group rather than the common one. No statement in the leaflet supports the claim that every patient has side effects, and immediate stopping is reserved for the rare effects, not for sleep disturbance.
questions.topic: Reading · medicine leaflet (frequency bands and urgent effects)

questions.stem:
"Street trees and small parks measurably cool dense neighbourhoods in summer. In a survey of ten Mediterranean cities, streets whose canopy covered more than 30% of the view from the pavement were on average 2.1 °C cooler on summer afternoons than otherwise similar streets with sparse canopy. The difference was largest in districts with low buildings and narrow streets, where shaded surfaces trap less heat. Cooling depended on species and on irrigation: unwatered young trees grew too slowly in dry summers to shade anything. City planners quoted in the report treat canopy as one instrument among several, alongside reflective roofs and lighter pavements."

From a newspaper report on urban climate research

Indicate which of the following statements is not correct:
options: Streets with more than 30% canopy cover were, on average, cooler than similar streets with sparse canopy in the survey.
How well trees cool a street can depend on the species and on whether the trees are watered.
Tree planting has been shown by the report to be a complete solution to summer heat in Mediterranean cities.
In districts with low buildings and narrow streets, the cooling difference associated with canopy was largest.
The report presents canopy as one of several instruments available to city planners.
questions.exp: The report describes canopy as one instrument among several, alongside reflective roofs and lighter pavements, so the statement claiming tree planting is a complete solution contradicts the passage and is the incorrect one. The other four statements restate the survey's comparisons, the role of species and irrigation, and the district effect faithfully.

questions.stem:
"In this country the ruler causes money to be made from the inner bark of mulberry trees, pressed into sheets like paper and cut into round pieces of different values. With this money everything can be bought throughout the whole empire. Refusing it is punishable, and every year the ruler causes all the mulberry bark that can be gathered to be bought up. It costs him almost nothing, yet with it he buys the goods of merchants from every land, who must accept it in exchange."

Adapted from The Travels of Marco Polo (13th century)

What does the passage describe?
options: Seashells used as currency
Gold coins stamped with the ruler's seal
Paper money issued by a ruler
Letters of credit drawn on banks
Barter between merchants and the ruler
questions.exp: The money is described as sheets pressed from mulberry bark, cut into pieces of different values and imposed as legal tender across the empire, which identifies it as state-issued paper money. Gold coins and letters of credit are different instruments, and barter contradicts the requirement that merchants accept the money in exchange.

questions.stem:
"Bacteria in the large intestine ferment fibres that human digestive enzymes cannot break down. The fermentation releases short-chain fatty acids, which are absorbed and used by the cells of the intestinal wall as an energy source. Some of these acids also enter the bloodstream and influence the activity of immune cells. The composition of the bacterial population differs between people and shifts with diet over weeks."

From a popular science book on the human body

Only one of the following statements is coherent with the excerpt:
options: Gut bacteria can convert dietary fibre into substances that the body absorbs and uses.
Human digestive enzymes release short-chain fatty acids from fibre in the small intestine.
The bacterial population of the intestine is fixed at birth and does not change with diet.
Short-chain fatty acids act only inside the intestinal lumen and never enter the blood.
Immune cell activity is independent of the products of gut bacteria.
questions.exp: The passage states that bacteria ferment fibre into short-chain fatty acids which are absorbed and used, some of them reaching the bloodstream and influencing immune cells, so the first statement is the coherent one. The claim that human enzymes do this in the small intestine contradicts the opening sentence, the fixed-population claim contradicts the shift with diet, and the last two claims reverse what is said about the bloodstream and immune cells.

questions.stem:
"Take this medicine at evenly spaced times as prescribed and complete the full course, even if your symptoms improve, because stopping early can let the infection return. If you forget a dose, take it as soon as you remember, but skip the missed dose if your next dose is due soon; never take a double dose. Return any unused tablets to a pharmacy: they must not be kept to treat future illnesses or given to other people."

From the informational leaflet for an antibiotic

Which of the following statements is the correct interpretation of the instructions?
options: Stopping the course when symptoms improve is the recommended way to avoid side effects.
Two tablets should be taken together whenever a dose is missed.
Leftover tablets must not be saved to treat a later illness.
This antibiotic should always be taken with food.
Sharing the medicine with a family member who has similar symptoms is acceptable.
questions.exp: The leaflet explicitly says unused tablets must be returned to a pharmacy and not kept for future illnesses or given to others, which matches the statement about leftovers. The full course is required even after symptoms improve, a missed dose is skipped rather than doubled, and nothing in the excerpt mentions taking the medicine with food.

questions.stem:
"In a large Spanish trial, volunteers at high cardiovascular risk were assigned by lottery to either a Mediterranean-style diet supplemented with extra-virgin olive oil and nuts, or to a control diet advised only to limit fat. Over about five years, the Mediterranean groups suffered roughly 30% fewer heart attacks, strokes and deaths from cardiovascular causes than the control group. The benefit appeared without meaningful weight loss and without a rise in calorie intake. The researchers note that the diet as a whole was tested, not any single ingredient, and that participants lived in a Mediterranean country where these foods are familiar and affordable."

From a newspaper report on nutrition research

Indicate which of the following statements is not correct:
options: Assignment to the Mediterranean or the control diet in the trial was random.
Major cardiovascular events were about 30% lower in the Mediterranean groups.
The trial demonstrated the protective effect of extra-virgin olive oil alone.
The benefit did not depend on the participants losing weight.
The researchers evaluated a whole dietary pattern rather than one ingredient.
questions.exp: The passage states that the diet as a whole was tested and not any single ingredient, so the claim that olive oil alone was shown to be protective is the incorrect one. The other statements restate the lottery assignment, the 30% reduction in events, the absence of weight-loss dependence and the whole-pattern evaluation.

questions.stem:
"With the telescope I have detected four small stars that have escaped the notice of every astronomer before me. They attend a certain planet, arranged in a straight line with it, and their distances from the planet change: at times one hides behind the planet or passes in front of it, and they complete their circuits in unequal periods, the nearest the fastest."

Adapted from Galileo Galilei, Sidereus Nuncius (1610)

What did the author observe?
options: Comets passing close to the Sun
Spots on the surface of the Sun
Fixed stars that never change position
Four moons orbiting a planet
The rings of Saturn
questions.exp: The objects follow a planet, pass behind and in front of it, and circuit it at different speeds like attendants, which identifies them as the four large moons of Jupiter observed by Galileo. Fixed stars do not orbit a planet, comets orbit the Sun, and neither sunspots nor rings match bodies that repeatedly disappear behind a planet in a straight line with it.
questions.topic: Reading · history of science source (Galileo's telescope)

questions.stem:
"An antibiotic kills susceptible bacteria but spares any cells that already carry resistance genes, for example a gene encoding an enzyme that destroys the drug. The surviving cells multiply, and resistance genes can also pass between bacteria on small circles of DNA. In environments where antibiotics are used often, such as hospitals, resistant strains therefore make up a growing share of the bacterial population over time."

From a microbiology textbook

Only one of the following statements is coherent with the excerpt:
options: Bacteria deliberately mutate when an antibiotic is present so that they can survive it.
Antibiotics create resistance genes inside susceptible bacteria.
Resistance genes can never move from one bacterium to another.
Frequent use of antibiotics favours the spread of resistant strains.
Susceptible and resistant cells are killed by an antibiotic to the same degree.
questions.exp: Because the drug spares cells that already carry resistance genes while killing susceptible ones, frequent antibiotic use selects for resistant strains, which then multiply and share genes, so the selection statement is the coherent one. Deliberate mutation and direct creation of genes are misreadings of selection, the passage says genes pass between bacteria on circles of DNA, and by definition susceptible cells are killed more than resistant ones.
